title: What happens where tectonic plates meet?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: What are the types of plate boundaries?
What happens when two plates collide?
What happens when plates pull apart?

explain.say: The edges where plates meet are called plate boundaries, and that is where most volcanoes, earthquakes and mountains are found.

draw.text: What happens where tectonic plates meet?

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: two plates meeting. Look at the ocean plate, the continental plate and the trench. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

draw.text: What happens where tectonic plates meet?

explain.say: Where plates pull apart, at divergent boundaries, magma rises into the gap and cools into new crust. This builds mid-ocean ridges, and Iceland sits on one.

explain.say: Where plates push together, at convergent boundaries, a heavy ocean plate sinks under the other in a process called subduction, making trenches and volcanoes. If two continents collide, they crumple into mountains like the Himalayas.

explain.say: At transform boundaries plates slide past each other sideways. No crust is made or destroyed, but the rock sticks and slips, causing earthquakes, as on the San Andreas Fault.

faq.q: What happens when plates pull apart?
faq.a: Magma rises into the gap and cools to make new crust. Under the sea this builds mid-ocean ridges; on land it makes rift valleys, like the East African Rift.

faq.q: What happens when two plates collide?
faq.a: If an ocean plate meets another plate, the heavier ocean plate sinks beneath it, making a deep trench and a line of volcanoes. If two continents collide, neither sinks easily, so the crust crumples into high mountains.
Subduction is when one plate dives beneath another into the mantle. Water released from the sinking plate helps the rock above melt, which feeds volcanoes.
asks: Why does one plate go under another?

faq.a: A transform boundary is where two plates slide past each other sideways. The San Andreas Fault in California is a famous example, and it causes many earthquakes.
asks: What happens when plates slide past each other?

faq.a: Iceland sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, where the North American and Eurasian plates pull apart, and also above a hot spot. Both feed lots of magma to the surface.
asks: Why does Iceland have so many volcanoes?

facts: The Mariana Trench, the deepest place in the ocean, formed where the Pacific plate sinks beneath the Philippine Sea plate.
Iceland sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, where two plates pull apart.
The Himalayas formed when the Indian plate collided with the Eurasian plate.

quiz.say: What kind of boundary formed the Himalayas?
quiz.why: The Indian plate crashed into the Eurasian plate, and the crust crumpled upward into mountains.

wrong.1: Pulling apart makes ridges and rift valleys, not huge fold mountains.
wrong.2: Sliding past makes faults and earthquakes, not big mountain ranges.
